ex_en: I have something I want to tell you.
note: pl. حاجات 7ājāt (حوايج 7wāyij means clothes/stuff). Very frequent filler word.

ex_en: I have a problem at work.
We have to find a solution to this matter.
I have a good idea.
What's your opinion of the house?
This is a chance that won't come again.

phrases.en: nice to meet you (lit. happy occasion)

ex_en: My luck isn't good today.
By God, you're lucky!
Tell me the truth.
That's a big lie.
note: pl. كذبات kidhbāt; كذب kidhb = lying (in general)

ex_en: What's the reason?
Forgive me, it was a mistake.
What's the difference between them?
What's the point of this talk?
note: pl. فوايد fawāyid; also 'interest' at a bank

ex_en: I have a habit of drinking coffee in the morning.
His condition has improved a bit.
The situation in the country is calm.
I want to talk with you about a matter.
The case is in court now.
Did you hear the news?
note: pl. أخبار akhbār (also 'the news' on TV)

ex_en: Tell me the story from the start.
I read a nice story.
This is a secret, don't tell anyone.

ex_ar: عندي ذكريات حلوة في الحوش هذا.
ex_en: I have sweet memories in this house.
I had a strange dream last night.
One must respect the elders.
note: Libyans also say قدر gadr for respect/esteem.

ex_en: Honour is a big thing for Libyans.

phrases.en: pleased to meet you (lit. we are honoured)

ex_en: Everyone has the freedom to choose.
We want peace in the country.
Safety is the most important thing.
Security has returned to the city.
He put a big effort into the work.
Life is hard these days.
The world has changed.
note: Also used for weather: الدنيا سخونة = it's hot.

ex_en: Living is expensive these days.
What's the meaning of this word?
This is your right.
I did it for your sake.
note: pl. خواطر khwāTir. على خاطر = because.

ex_en: His intention is good.

phrases.en: as you intend; you'll get what you intend

ex_en: This thing has no value.
This matter is very important.
I think about the children's future.
Leave the past in the past.
It was a tough experience.
He has ten years of experience.
Congratulations on your success!
Failure isn't the end of the world.
A disaster happened in the neighbourhood.
The flood was a catastrophe.
Everything is fate and destiny.
note: Used a lot about marriage. pl. أنصبة anSiba.

ex_en: This is God's apportioning.

ex_ar: هذا مكتوب، ما فيش هروب منه.
ex_tr: hādha maktūb, ma fīsh hrūb minnah.
ex_en: It's written; there's no escaping it.
We believe in divine decree and destiny.
note: Not to be confused with قدر gidir (cooking pot).

ex_en: I have doubts about what he says.
I don't trust him.
Dignity before everything.
How embarrassing! What did you do?
This is a disgrace in front of people.
He has a good reputation in the market.
I want a bit of rest.
Too much jealousy ruins things.
I long for home a lot.
Missing people is hard.
She doesn't speak out of shyness.
I'm only asking out of curiosity.
He has big ambitions.

phrases.en: my ambition is to finish my studies

ex_en: What's your goal in life?
note: pl. أهداف ahdāf. For football goal Libyans say قول gōl.

ex_en: What's our plan?
Teach me the method.
Which type do you want?
Part of the money was lost.
note: pl. أجزاء ajzā'. Also one of the 30 parts of the Quran.

phrases.en: the last part of the Quran

ex_en: Give me an example.
Now it's your turn.
I'm in difficult circumstances.
note: pl. ظروف DHurūf (mostly used in plural). Also 'envelope'.

ex_en: This is your responsibility.
The road is dangerous at night.
Everyone looks after his own interest.
Our relationship is good.

phrases.en: how are you related to him?
it's nothing to do with me

ex_en: What's my fault?
You have no excuse.
There's a blessing in this house.
They built a new mosque in the neighbourhood.
note: pl. مساجد masājid. Everyday word is جامع jāmi3.

ex_en: The imam has a beautiful voice.
I do my ablutions and pray.
note: Usually said with درّ (to do) or توضى (to perform ablution).

phrases.en: are you in a state of ablution?

ex_en: We paid the zakat on the money.
I gave the fitra alms before the Eid prayer.
note: Libyans often call zakat al-fitr simply الفطرة.

ex_en: My mother went for umrah in Ramadan.
After iftar we go to tarawih prayers.
note: Plural form; singular ترويحة is rare.

ex_en: Today's sermon was long.
note: pl. خطب khuTab. Do not confuse with خطوبة (engagement).

ex_en: My grandfather always has prayer beads in his hand.
note: pl. سبح sibe7; also مسبحة misb7a

phrases.en: he counts praises on the beads

ex_en: The pilgrims circle the Kaaba.

ex_ar: نبي نمشي لمكة قبل ما نموت.
ex_tr: nibbi nimshi l-makka gbal ma nmūt.
ex_en: I want to go to Mecca before I die.
Which way is the qibla here?
The dawn prayer is two rak'as.
I prayed the obligatory prayer on time.
Giving charity is a Sunna.
Ramadan is a month of worship.
The door of repentance is open.
May God reward you.
A good deed is rewarded tenfold.

phrases.en: do it as a good deed

ex_en: There's great reward in it.
This is something forbidden.
note: Exists in the deck as an exclamation; this card is the noun sense.

ex_en: Pray istikhara before you decide.
She went to the sheikh to recite healing verses over her.
note: Common practice in Libya against envy and evil eye.

ex_en: Put the Quran copy on top of the shelf.
He memorised a new sura today.
He recited the Throne Verse.
note: pl. آيات āyāt. Also 'a marvel': آية في الجمال.

en: al-Fatiha; recitation to seal an agreement
ex_en: We recited al-Fatiha for his soul.
note: In Libya reciting the Fatiha also seals an engagement.

ex_en: There's a hadith that says so.
Pray for the Prophet (calm down).
note: pl. أنبياء anbiyā. 'صلي على النبي' is said to calm someone.

ex_en: The Messenger of God said…
His faith is strong.
May God have mercy on his soul.
note: pl. أرواح arwā7. Also 'self': روحي = myself.

ex_en: May God admit you to paradise.
It's hell in the summer.
We work for this world and the hereafter.
Am I to wait for you till Judgment Day?

phrases.en: signs of the end of days

ex_en: He's sleeping like an angel.
note: pl. ملايكة malāyka. Not ملك malik (king).

ex_en: I seek refuge in God from Satan.
note: pl. شياطين shayāTīn. Also a naughty child.

ex_en: My grandmother tells us stories about the jinn.
This is from envy (the evil eye).
note: Libyans say ما شاء الله to ward it off; also called العين.

ex_en: She burned incense in the house.
note: Burned at weddings, Fridays and against the evil eye.

ex_en: May God have mercy on the martyrs.
The funeral is after the afternoon prayer.
We visited my grandfather's grave.
Did they see the crescent? Is Eid tomorrow?
note: The sighting of the crescent decides when Ramadan and Eid begin.

ex_ar: ليلة القدر الناس الكل في الجوامع.
ex_tr: lēlat il-qadr in-nās il-kull fi l-jwāmi3.
ex_en: On the Night of Power everyone is at the mosques.
note: In Libya kids often get new clothes and girls get henna on the 27th.

phrases.en: prayer on the Night of Power

ex_en: On Ashura they make dried meat dishes.
note: Libyans cook dishes with قديد (cured meat) from Eid al-Adha.

ex_en: Imsak is at half past four.
Fasting in summer is hard.
note: Same meaning as صوم; صيام is more common in religious talk.

phrases.en: the six days of Shawwal fast

ex_en: I can't drink, I'm fasting.
note: fem. صايمة Sāyma; pl. صايمين Sāymīn

ex_en: Libyan hospitality is famous.
Generosity is one of our customs.

en: invitation to a meal; dinner party
ex_ar: عندنا عزومة الليلة في حوش خالي.
ex_en: We have a dinner invitation tonight at my uncle's.
He held a big banquet for the wedding.

phrases.en: he slaughtered and held a feast

ex_en: On Friday we have a picnic at the beach.
note: Libyan/Maghrebi word for a festive outing with a big meal.

ex_en: I brought you a gift on the occasion of your success.
This is a gift for you.
We had visitors yesterday.
Thanks for the invitation.
note: pl. دعوات da3wāt. دعوة أمي = my mother's blessing/prayer.

ex_en: Pass on greetings from your friend to me.
Their engagement is next week.

ex_ar: الملاك يوم الخميس والعرس بعد شهر.
ex_tr: il-mlāk yōm il-khmīs w-il-3ers ba3d shahr.
ex_en: The marriage contract is Thursday and the wedding a month later.
note: Libyan word for the signing of the marriage contract (عقد القران).

ex_en: Dowries are expensive these days.

ex_ar: العروسة قاعدة تشري في الجهاز متاعها.
ex_tr: il-3arūsa gā3da tishri fi j-jhāz mtā3ha.
ex_en: The bride is buying her trousseau.
She put henna on her hands for Eid.
The old ladies let out ululations.
We preserve our traditions.
Malouf is part of our heritage.
Libyan culture is a mix.
The Libyan dialect has Italian words.
As the proverb says…
note: pl. أمثال amthāl. Not مثل mithl (like).

ex_en: He told us a funny joke.
My grandfather has great wisdom.
He loves folk poetry.
His uncle is a well-known poet.
He said it as a ghnawat 3alam.
note: Bedouin genre (غناوة العلم): a one-line sung poem of love or longing.

phrases.en: he knows lots of ghnawa lines

ex_en: At the wedding they played marskawi.
note: Popular Libyan wedding music genre, originally from the east/south.

ex_en: He loves art and drawing.
He's a well-known artist in Libya.
note: pl. فنانين fannānīn; in Libya often means a singer.

ex_en: My daughter loves drawing.
note: pl. رسوم rsūm (also fees: رسوم التسجيل).

ex_en: We hung a painting in the living room.
note: pl. لوحات lō7āt. Also number plate (لوحة السيارة).

ex_en: We went to the theatre to see a play.
note: pl. مسارح masāri7; a play is مسرحية masra7iyya.

ex_ar: في العرس فيه رقص لنص الليل.
ex_tr: fi l-3ers fīh rugS l-nuSS il-lēl.
ex_en: At the wedding there's dancing till midnight.
Did you hear the drum? There's a wedding.
He knows how to play the darbuka.
My uncle plays the oud.
They brought a band for the wedding.
There's a festival in the Old City.
We went to the book fair.
Leptis Magna has Roman ruins.
Libya has ancient civilizations.
